chapter: Al Hibbler, Dakota Staton and later years
title: Charlie Byrd's club, Joe Williams and Chicago, then Washington after 1965
summary: He plays two years in Pete Lambros's club with Byrd, tours with Joe Williams, then stays around Washington.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Anyway, after that, I flew back to Washington, and I started working in a club that was owned by a fellow named Pete Lambros, but the main attraction there was a guitarist whose name was Charlie Byrd. I worked up there for I guess the better part of two years. But while I was there, I did some other miscellaneous engagements with people, one of them being Joe Williams. I did a thing, I was back in California again with him. We were there for something like two or three weeks.

After that we did a club in Chicago, called I think Basin Street. I had a trio there, I believe... Yeah, I sent to Washington and I got a bass player Fred Williams, and a drummer, Harold Chavis. I think we had a couple of weeks there in Chicago which proved to be pretty nice.

After that... I guess this is about up to 1965. Since then, everything has been pretty much around Washington, D.C. There have been groups and there have been trios, and a lot of things that I've done here with the better musicians around Washington.
